🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-20 23:00 → 2026-10-21 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Claim-aware escrow experiment opened** — Pavlo opened a Draft PR routing authorization through execution verdicts to gate an escrow contract, testing a concrete downstream use case for the claim pipeline. [PR #8](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/8)

> **Cryptographer joins zkIE** — A cryptographer focused on zkIE joined the group, strengthening the independent-verification work with new domain expertise. [tg:tawg:5646]

> **Transformer study notes landed** — A complete Transformer study series was committed to the shared contribution repository, expanding the group's accessible technical reference material. [commit ca64ea7](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/commit/ca64ea7182f7a02fa9f7a869f8e9f05f0b0d146a)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### verifiable-execution-claim-authorization

_The research series covered new ground across replay composition, obligation coverage, external consumers, and verdict-gated escrow._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Opened** a draft connecting claim-aware authorization to a verdict-gated escrow in invinoveritas, testing how execution verdicts can govern downstream access control and exposing authorization gaps that standard integration tests miss. [tg:tawg:5647]
- Pavlo **Shipped** an experiment pairing real-artifact composition with explicit execution limits, clarifying how boundaries affect whether a claim remains valid. [PR #2](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/2)
- Pavlo **Shipped** an experiment composing claim-aware replay with independent admission review, confirming both paths remain coherent when claim logic is layered on top. [PR #7](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/7)
- Pavlo **Published** scenario-relative verification obligation coverage research that separates per-scenario obligations from global ones, giving reviewers a structured map of what each execution path must prove. [PR #4](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/4)
- Baby Blue Viper **Extended** the v4.1 research line with checker-independence and authorization-scope binding, keeping the O14 checker neutral across varied claim evaluations. [PR #5](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/5)
- Pavlo **Added** a claim-aware ERC-8404 consumer that attaches from the outside without touching core, giving adopters a path forward that avoids upstream protocol changes. [PR #6](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/6)

### zkIE community

_The zkIE direction gained a new collaborator, a conference opportunity, and a cross-group design discussion all in a single day._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Connected** the Guarantee Composition experiment to a potential ETH Shenzhen showcase, creating an opportunity to introduce zkIE's approach to a wider audience of developers and researchers. [tg:tawg:5641]
- Baby Blue Viper **Welcomed** Asher and articulated how the TAWG's signed-verdict approach complements zkIE's goals, helping orient a new collaborator toward the shared verification mission from day one. [tg:tawg:5642]
- Asher li (@asher40404) **Joined** the group as a cryptographer focused on zkIE and expressed interest in connecting independent verification work to downstream applications, widening the team's view of how verdicts travel through a system. [tg:tawg:5646]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Reviewed** Pavlo's evaluation paradigm and test matrix, noted that it surfaces subtle authorization gaps, and proposed a general Agent Conformance Harness to help the wider community detect semantic drift. [tg:tawg:5653]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Engaged** with the Agent Conformance Harness idea by exploring how it could catch semantic drift that ordinary integration tests miss, keeping the concept alive for future development. [tg:tawg:5654]

### learning resources

_The contribution repository gained a structured study reference for a foundational neural architecture._

- Jimmy Shi **Added** a complete Transformer study notes series to the contribution repository, offering a zero-to-full English walkthrough that builds shared technical vocabulary across the group. [commit ca64ea7](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/commit/ca64ea7182f7a02fa9f7a869f8e9f05f0b0d146a)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Agent Conformance Harness concept raised in cross-review — worth prototyping as a shared tool for semantic drift detection across agent implementations
- ETH Shenzhen as a venue for a zkIE and Guarantee Composition presentation to a broader developer audience

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review Draft PR #8 on claim-aware authorization to verdict-gated escrow
- Explore how Asher's cryptography background can strengthen the signed-verdict and independent-verification pipeline
- Assess PRs #2, #4, #6, #7 for review readiness and integration into the main research track

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A new cryptographer joined just as the authorization research opened into verdict-gated escrow territory — fresh expertise arrived exactly when the design space needed it most.
>
> Research PRs, study notes, and a new collaborator all landing in one day: the group's conveyor belt is clearly running at full speed. 🤖
